article_title: Dior Sauvage Alternatives From Real Fragrance Houses, Not Clones
scope: Dior Sauvage EDP composition per Dior's own pages; reliable popularity/market-position claims about Sauvage; reputable definitions of clone/dupe vs. original; reputable definitions of the fougere, aromatic, fresh spicy and citrus note families. No performance claims (longevity/projection/compliments) recorded as fact.

claims.claim: Dior's own FAQ copy describes Sauvage Eau de Parfum's full note structure: top note Calabrian bergamot, heart notes Sichuan pepper/lavender/star anise, base notes Papua New Guinea vanilla extract and ambroxan.
claims.quote: Dior Sauvage Eau de Parfum opens with a burst of Calabrian bergamot — bright, fresh and citrusy — before revealing warm heart notes of Sichuan pepper, lavender, and star anise. The dry-down settles into a rich, sensual base of vanilla extract from Papua New Guinea and ambroxan that leave a smoky, magnetic trail.

claims.claim: Dior's product description states the EDP centers on a Calabrian bergamot top note paired with a Papua New Guinean vanilla extract accord.
claims.quote: Sauvage Eau de Parfum teams the freshness of a juicy, spicy Calabrian bergamot note with the sensuality of a mysterious and enveloping Papua New Guinean vanilla extract accord to unfurl a powerful and noble trail.

claims.claim: Dior names and describes the specific bergamot material used in Sauvage EDP as Reggio di Calabria bergamot.
claims.quote: This bergamot is a whirlwind of juicy freshness that seems to sweep up everything in its trail. Drenched in the Calabrian sun, it is fruitier than other bergamots and develops slightly peppery and zesty facets.

claims.claim: Dior names and describes the specific vanilla material used in Sauvage EDP as Papua New Guinean vanilla extract, harvested and processed via a solvent-free method.
claims.quote: Papua New Guinean vanilla extract unfurls an irresistibly delicious attraction with smoky accents that render it more virile. Harvested green and then scalded, this exceptional vanilla is processed using a solvent-free extraction method to restore the complex power of its aromas while preserving the environment.

claims.claim: Dior markets Sauvage EDP as one of its most popular gifting choices (a company self-description of popularity, not an independent ranking).
claims.quote: Dior Sauvage Eau de Parfum is one of the most popular gifting choices in the Dior men's fragrance collection — perfect for birthdays, Father's Day and anniversaries.

claims.claim: Trade press reports the Sauvage franchise ranks first among all fragrances (masculine and feminine combined) a decade after its 2015 launch, the only men's scent to hold that claim.
claims.quote: Dior Sauvage men's scent ranks first among all fragrances — masculine and feminine combined — 10 years after its launch. It is the only men's scent to make that claim. Currently, one bottle is snapped up every 30 seconds and more than 12 million of those are rung up yearly.

claims.claim: Parfums Christian Dior's CEO is on record calling Sauvage the world's bestselling item in fragrance.
claims.quote: “It’s by far the world’s bestselling item today in the fragrance business,” said Véronique Courtois, chief executive officer of Parfums Christian Dior.

claims.claim: Dior's CEO states Sauvage has held the number-one fragrance position (not just men's fragrance) globally every year since 2021.
claims.quote: Sauvage has held that pole position annually since 2021. “It’s not only the number one men’s fragrance sold in the world,” she underlined. “It’s the number-one fragrance sold in the world.”

claims.claim: The Sauvage line's Eau de Parfum expression launched in 2018, a year after the original Eau de Toilette (2015); Parfum followed in 2019.
claims.quote: The Sauvage line was expanded with more products. After the Eau de Toilette came the Eau de Parfum in 2018 and Parfum in 2019.

claims.claim: The original Sauvage Eau de Toilette became the top-selling men's fragrance globally in 2018.
claims.quote: Sauvage Eau de Toilette began selling a decade ago strongly in numerous markets, including the U.K., and became the top-selling men’s scent globally in 2018.

claims.claim: A NPR (reputable press) report distinguishes fragrance dupes from counterfeits: dupes are marketed openly as 'inspired by' the original rather than passed off as the branded product.
claims.quote: These aren't knock-offs claiming to be brand-name perfume. Companies that make dupes openly advertise them as being "inspired by" more expensive alternatives.

claims.claim: A Brussels-based perfumer quoted by NPR says the closest dupes can be difficult even for professionals to distinguish from the original.
claims.quote: "Some of the dupes are so close to their original that even professionals would have difficulty telling them apart," said Victoria Belim-Frolova, a perfumer based in Brussels.

claims.claim: NPR reports the technical method (GCMS) fragrance makers use to reverse-engineer a competitor's formula when building a dupe.
claims.quote: Fragrance makers have long used a technology called gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GCMS) to identify the specific molecules in a competitor's fragrance – a crucial step to creating a believable dupe.

claims.claim: Wikipedia's encyclopedic definition of the fougere family: a classic top-note lavender / base-note oakmoss-and-coumarin structure.
claims.quote: Fougère perfumes are made with a blend of fragrances: top-notes are sweet, with the scent of lavender flowers; as the more volatile components evaporate, the scents of oakmoss, derived from a species of lichen and described as woody, sharp and slightly sweet, and coumarin, similar to the scent of new-mown hay, become noticeable.

claims.claim: Wikipedia defines 'aromatic fougere' as a derivative of the classic fougere structure with added herb, spice and/or wood notes.
claims.quote: aromatic fougère, a derivative of this class, contains additional notes of herbs, spice and/or wood

claims.claim: Wikipedia dates the fougere genre's origin to 1882 with Houbigant's Fougère Royale.
claims.quote: The fougère genre was established in 1882 with the creation of Fougère Royale for Houbigant.

claims.claim: The Perfume Society (UK fragrance trade organization) defines the fougere family by its typical material list.
claims.quote: Nowadays, it's mostly fragrances for men you'll find in the fougère category, which almost invariably feature lavender, geranium, vetiver, bergamot, oakmoss and coumarin in the blend.

claims.claim: Jomashop (established fragrance/luxury retailer) defines the aromatic family as built around earthy, spicy, uplifting herbal and botanical notes such as lavender, rosemary, basil and sage.
claims.quote: In perfumery, the term “aromatic” refers to scents built around herbal and botanical notes that are earthy, spicy, and uplifting. These perfumes often include ingredients like lavender, rosemary, basil, and sage — creating a profile that feels clean, natural, and refreshing.

claims.claim: The Perfume Society's 'Fresh Aromatic' subfamily description: herbal notes (tarragon, thyme, rosemary) alongside citrus elements, skewing masculine.
claims.quote: More masculine than feminine, this group: herbal, aromatic notes – tarragon, thyme, rosemary – play alongside the citrussy elements. They're airy and outdoorsy.

claims.claim: The Perfume Society defines the Fresh family (which houses citrus/cologne fragrances) by its characteristic citrus notes.
claims.quote: Uplifting, zesty, cooling: most eau de Colognes fall into this family. They feature a whoosh of notes like lemon, bergamot, orange, grapefruit, mandarin.

claims.claim: The Perfume Society's dedicated Citrus subfamily page notes its shared, unisex character.
claims.quote: Often these can be 'shared': equally suited to men and women, with a simple elegance and crispness.

claims.claim: A fragrance retailer's descriptive definition of the 'fresh spicy' family: freshness (citrus, herbs, air) combined with spice warmth (cinnamon, pepper, cardamom). Lower-authority source; use for directional description only.
claims.quote: Fresh and spicy aromas combine the freshness of the notes with the warm caress of spices. They can be uplifting and still cozy... The “fresh” part has to do with appealing scents. Think citrus fruits, fresh herbs, or air. The “spicy” part adds warmth and depth, often through the introduction of spices like cinnamon, pepper, or cardamom.

dropped.claim: A single, independently reputable source that cleanly defines 'clone' as a term distinct from 'dupe' (rather than treating them as synonyms or brand marketing language).
dropped.reason: Fragrantica community forum thread (fragrantica.com/board/viewtopic.php?id=272695) has multiple users giving conflicting, informal definitions (some treat clone=dupe, others don't) — not a reputable/authoritative source. ALT Fragrances' and Maple Prime's FAQ definitions come from dupe-selling brands themselves (self-interested marketing copy), so excluded as unreliable for a neutral definition. Used NPR's neutral dupe-vs-counterfeit framing instead, which does not use the word 'clone.'
